title: Keep plan-read requests in the plan and drain queue; fix --budget room
summary: Retry of the rejected fix. Requests read by `athena plan` must stay in the plan and drain's queue (queued_work currently lists only Queued), and plan's room check in Drain::prepare must reserve only the read cap so the default --budget 2 reads. The audience is the operator running plan then drain. The retry also fixes the earlier misses: criterion 7 had no recorded commands, a running-job test faked state, and README wrapping was uneven.

defaults_applied.how: New named tests plus cargo test, clippy and fmt --check criteria.
Criteria check plan and drain behavior through tests, not wiring.
Fix queued_work's queue rule and the room check, not just the observed case.
Handover must cite commands that ran, as the last verdict demanded.
One focused change on the plan/drain queue.
Docs and CHANGELOG written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The typed request 'try again' takes precedence: redo the original plan/drain fix, not the proposed pre-handover evidence-check feature.
Goal is that an operator who runs `athena plan --budget N` then `athena drain` sees read requests still open and worked in plan order.
Read cap is the reader_usd config value; plan at default budget 2.0 must be able to afford one read.
The producer must run cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check on the final state and record the exact commands and results in its handover.
No governance file changes are needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test queues requests on a drained channel, runs plan with a budget that reads some (stub reader), and shows the read requests remain in the plan entries and in queue() with read=true. Run cargo test.
A test shows that after a plan that reads requests, drain still works them: they are in its queue, not read again, and run in plan order. Run cargo test.
A second plan after the first lists the same open requests, not 'nothing is open'. Run cargo test.

A test runs plan at the default budget (2.0) with the repo's reader_usd/job_usd values, shows it reads at least one request and keeps it queued; Drain::prepare's room check reserves only the read cap for plan. Run cargo test.

Separate named tests through queued_work over real records show these stay out of the queue: a read request on a non-drained channel, a closed job, a declined job, and a running job. The running-job test uses a genuinely dispatched-but-unfinished record, not outcome fields cleared in memory. Run cargo test.
A test over real records with a work decision approving a Proposed job on a drained channel shows it is listed exactly once. Run cargo test.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check all pass, and the handover cites each exact command that ran with its exit status and output tail.
The misleading test name in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (the_plan_of_a_read_job_names_a_missing_path_...) is replaced or backed by a test that really reads the job first.

queued_work doc comment, drain.rs module text, README and CHANGELOG describe the new queue rule and the corrected --budget meaning; README paragraphs are re-wrapped to the neighbouring line width with no early breaks.

out_of_scope: A new pre-handover evidence-check mechanism in the build pipeline
Changes to the reader, verifier or other commands beyond plan/drain queue handling
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than reference: the prior attempt touched five files across core and cli, and one criterion needs a real dispatched-job fixture.
